question.prompt: Let \(f\) be a function defined on the set of positive rational numbers with the property that \(f(a\cdot b) = f(a) + f(b)\) for all positive rational numbers \(a\) and \(b.\) Suppose that \(f\) also has the property that \(f(p) = p\) for every prime number \(p.\) For which of the following numbers \(x\) is \(f(x) \lt 0?\)

solutions.title: Evaluate using prime factors
solutions.explanation:
The product rule lets us compute \(f\) from prime factors, counting each repeated factor separately. First,
\[
f(1)=f(1\cdot1)=2f(1),
\]
so \(f(1)=0\). For every positive rational number \(r\),
\[
0=f(r\cdot r^{-1})=f(r)+f(r^{-1}),
\]
which gives \(f(r^{-1})=-f(r)\). Thus
\[
f\left(\frac ab\right)=f(a)-f(b).
\]
Also, repeated use of the product rule gives \(f(p^k)=kp\) for a prime \(p\) and positive integer \(k\).

Factoring the numbers in the choices now gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
f\left(\frac{17}{32}\right)&=17-5\cdot2=7,\\
f\left(\frac{11}{16}\right)&=11-4\cdot2=3,\\
f\left(\frac79\right)&=7-2\cdot3=1,\\
f\left(\frac76\right)&=7-2-3=2,\\
f\left(\frac{25}{11}\right)&=2\cdot5-11=-1.
\end{aligned}
\]
Only \(\boxed{\frac{25}{11}}\) gives a negative value, so the answer is choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
